messages:
Emily S: Hi team — escalation from Acme Health (prod org). Mobile users hitting repeated SSO reauth prompts when switching networks (cellular -> wifi). Customer says session shows as active in app but first API call after network change returns 401 and user is forced to reauth. Reported ~30% of mobile sessions for a single region.

Tanvi R: Thanks Emily — do we have a sample request/response and session id? Sounds like a device_assertion or session cookie rejection. Any recent org-level policy changes (IP bind / device_jwt TTL)? @oncall FYI. :eyes: 

Emily S: Pasting the curl from their mobile SDK (sanitized):

```
curl -i -H "Cookie: session=eyJhbGci...; device_jwt=eyJkaXZ..." 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <masked>" 
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Date: Tue, 12 Nov 2025 14:22:33 GMT
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"invalid_device_assertion","message":"device_assertion aud mismatch"}
```

Emily S: Session cookie TTL still valid per customer (checked). They say it only happens after network handoff; switching back to original network sometimes restores the session.

Lee O: Quick thoughts — could be our edge IP affinity + org configured to IP-bind sessions. When the source IP changes, auth server rejects device_assertion because the bound IP stored at issuance doesn't match the new IP. Do we have an org policy on "session_ip_bind" for Acme Health?

Alisa G: I'll check auth logs for that org. Also there's been a device-trust cert rotation two days ago; if the mobile SDK has an older cached thumbprint it might produce assertions with stale kid and cause aud validation failures. 

dev-bot: Created escalation ACME-342 and added severity=P1, owner=Tanvi R, runbook=https://redwood.internal/runbooks/auth/device-trust

Tanvi R: Emily — can you ask the customer for a base64 of the device_assertion JWT (header+payload only) so we can inspect aud/iss/kid without their private. Also confirm whether they use our embedded SDK or their own jwt mint.

Emily S: Sent a secure upload link to their eng lead. Repro steps from customer (copied):
1) Login on mobile over carrier network.
2) Background app, switch to wifi.
3) Open app and call /v1/generate -> 401 immediate.
4) Close app, reopen -> 200 (so cold start sometimes fixes).

Alisa G: From auth logs: I can see several device_assertion tokens with aud=acme-prod-api but our current validating service expects aud=redwood-device-assertion. That mismatch would explain the error. Two possibilities: (a) old SDK minted assertion with legacy aud, or (b) our audience expectation changed during a rollout.

Lee O: If the cold restart fixes it intermittently, it suggests the SDK is caching a token or using a cached assertion that gets refreshed on full restart. Network change could trigger a code path that reuses the cached device_jwt.

Tanvi R: Short-term mitigation: add a compatibility check to accept the legacy aud for Acme Health while we validate. I'll open a controlled-sidecar change for that org. Medium-term: get customer to update SDK or rotate audience mapping.

Emily S: Customer can ship an updated SDK only next week — they asked for a patch or config flip. I'll get them to reproduce and upload the assertion.

Alisa G: Two action items from auth side: 1) Dump timeline of audience validation changes from the auth service (last 7 days). 2) If we decide to accept legacy aud for this org, we need revocation checks and a scoped rollout.

Tanvi R: I'll schedule a quick mitigation rollout to accept legacy aud for ACME-342 and monitor metrics. Please hold any org-wide audience relax changes.

Emily S: Noted. I'll create a secure meeting with Acme engineering for 9am PST tomorrow and share repro artifacts.

Lee O: Also verify whether their edge (APN provider / carrier nat) rewrites headers or strips forwarded headers — sometimes X-Forwarded-For inconsistencies cause our IP-bind checks to trip.

Emily S: Good call. I've asked them to capture tcpdump and SDK logs.

Tanvi R: Thanks all — tagging incident channel for visibility. I'll post a short postmortem template once the root cause is confirmed. :thumbsup:

Emily S: Will update thread with the uploaded assertion and customer's tcpdump once I have them. Thanks team!
